# Results — Study 745 (Corporate-Jet-Index)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim — **David Yermack's
*Flights of Fancy* (2006): firms disclosing CEO personal use of the company aircraft
underperform by ~4%/yr** — tested as a monthly, equal-weight **long/short characteristic
sort**: long a basket of frugal-reputation large-caps, short a basket with a documented
CEO personal-aircraft red flag (each flyer entering only *after* its perk is public). We
judge the spread in **excess of the market** (SPY) with a **Newey-West (HAC)** *t*, and
as a **market-model alpha** to strip out beta. True governance-perk panels aren't free, so
firms come from a **hardcoded, labelled table** of ~24 large-caps. Offline core + synthetic
control are deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance **monthly** closes, `auto_adjust=True` → **total return** (dividends reinvested) — each firm + SPY |
| Perk table | hardcoded `JET_FIRMS` (ticker, heavy/low, public-year, note), fingerprint **ad201b5ed46c** |
| As-of | 2026-06-30 (last complete month; no partial bar) |
| Firms | **24** priced — **12 heavy** (jet red flag) / **12 low** (frugal peer) |
| Panel window | **2011-01 → 2026-06**, **186 months** (kept where both baskets have ≥4 eligible names) |
| Benchmark | SPY (market model `LS = α + β·SPY`); excess-of-market spread |
| Execution / lag | a heavy name is shortable only from **Jan of the year after** its perk is public (no look-ahead) |
| Costs | one-way **10 bps** × ~10%/mo turnover on **both** legs + **50 bps/yr** short borrow on the heavy leg |

> **Two named caveats (on the Signal axis).** (1) **Survivorship — and it points *against*
> the claim.** The archetypal jet abusers (Tyco/Kozlowski, WorldCom/Ebbers, Enron,
> Chesapeake/McClendon, Adelphia/Rigas) delisted to ~zero and cannot enter a yfinance tape,
> so the survivor-only heavy basket is *missing exactly the disasters Yermack's thesis
> predicts* — a survivor tape that still can't find the short is a conservative refutation.
> (2) The **heavy/low label** is the believers' own framing (Yermack's "flights of fancy")
> and is subjective at the margin. Neither moves the verdict.

## The signal — long/short (low − heavy), excess of market

| statistic | value |
|---|--:|
| LS mean (annualised) | **+2.11%/yr** |
| **HAC (Newey-West) *t*** | **+0.47** (lags 4) · naive iid *t* = 0.48 |
| annualised Sharpe | 0.12 |
| heavy basket excess-of-market | **−0.34%/yr** |
| low basket excess-of-market | **+1.76%/yr** |

The tradable spread is **indistinguishable from zero** (HAC *t* = 0.47). The frugal basket
edges the market, the flyer basket edges *below* it — the sign Yermack predicts — but the
gap drowns in its own standard error.

## Raw compounding — the flyers *did* lag the frugal peers

| basket | CAGR (total return, 2011-01 → 2026-06) |
|---|--:|
| **low-perk** (frugal) | **+16.15%/yr** |
| SPY | +14.17%/yr |
| **heavy-perk** (flyers) | **+12.19%/yr** |

Directionally consistent with the thesis: the frugal basket compounded ~4pp/yr ahead of
the flyers. But the monthly *spread* is far too noisy for that gap to clear significance —
and *why* it exists is the whole question, answered next.

## Alpha vs beta — the only significant number is a beta artifact

| statistic | value |
|---|--:|
| market-model **α** (annualised) | **+8.81%/yr** |
| **HAC *t* on α** | **+2.10** |
| long/short **β** to SPY | **−0.45** |
| heavy-basket β | **1.31** |
| low-basket β | **0.87** |

The one statistic that clears *t* = 2 is the CAPM alpha — and it is **manufactured by the
negative beta**. The frugal basket is low-beta defensive staples/retail (β ≈ 0.87); the
flyer basket is high-beta growth (β ≈ 1.31). Long-low/short-high is a **−0.45-beta**
book; in a bull market a short-beta portfolio earns a positive CAPM intercept **by
construction**. This is the Frazzini-Pedersen *betting-against-beta* / low-vol premium
wearing a jet costume — not a governance discount. Strip beta out via the raw spread and
the *t* collapses to 0.47.

## The founder-growth confound — Tesla alone flips the short basket

Heavy-name excess-of-market returns (annualised, from each name's eligibility date):

| the flyers that *lagged* | ex-mkt | | the flyers that *won* | ex-mkt |
|---|--:|---|---|--:|
| IEP (Icahn) | −14.1% | | **TSLA (Musk)** | **+53.5%** |
| CMCSA | −7.5% | | GOOGL | +10.1% |
| OXY | −5.7% | | META | +7.4% |
| LVS | −5.3% | | ANF | +4.7% |
| WYNN | −4.8% | | GE | +1.9% |
| DIS | −3.9% | | ORCL | +1.6% |

Most flyers *did* lag — but the surviving heavy basket is polluted by **founder-led growth
compounders** (Tesla, Alphabet, Meta, Oracle) whose jets are incidental to a growth tilt.
Drop those four and the heavy basket underperforms the market by **−3.83%/yr** (low
+1.76%/yr, LS **+5.80%/yr**) — *strikingly close to Yermack's −4%* — yet the spread is
**still only HAC *t* = 1.08**, and its alpha (*t* = 2.22, β = −0.41) is the same low-beta
artifact. The sign survives; the significance does not.

## The tradable version — net of costs and borrow

| | annualised |
|---|--:|
| gross LS | **+2.11%/yr** |
| − rebalance costs (both legs) | −0.24%/yr |
| − short borrow (heavy leg, 50 bps) | −0.50%/yr |
| **net LS** | **+1.36%/yr** (HAC *t* ≈ 0.5) |

A ~1.4%/yr net spread at *t* ≈ 0.5 is not an edge; it is a low-beta bet you could buy
cheaper and cleaner as an explicit low-vol factor, with none of the single-name jet risk
(one Tesla flips the sign).

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, and honest under the null

A deterministic monthly long/short panel (12 heavy / 12 low, equal betas) with a
**plantable heavy-basket discount**:

| planted heavy discount | LS mean (annualised) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| **0 bps/mo** (no edge) | −1.17% | **−0.49** |
| **−80 bps/mo** (≈ −9.2%/yr, large) | +8.76% | **+3.53** |

With **no** planted discount the HAC test stays below \|*t*\| = 2 (no false positive from
186 months); a large planted discount drives it to *t* = 3.5. The measurement engine
recovers a real governance discount when one exists — the real tape's *t* = 0.47 is what an
*absent-or-tiny, survivor-suppressed, beta-confounded* effect looks like.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The *sign* matches Yermack (frugal basket CAGR **16.2%** vs flyers
  **12.2%**; ex-mega-cap flyers lag the market **−3.8%/yr**, echoing his −4%), and
  **survivorship biases *against* the claim** (the delisted abusers are missing). But on the
  tradable spread the **HAC *t* = 0.47** (1.08 ex-mega-cap) — **fails *t* ≥ 2** — and the
  only significant statistic (+8.8%/yr α, *t* = 2.10) is a **−0.45-beta artifact**, not a
  governance premium. Literature + correct sign, sub-2 tape ⇒ weak, not real.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net **+1.4%/yr** at *t* ≈ 0.5, and it is a low-beta / low-vol
  bet dressed as governance — **one Tesla flips the short basket**. Nothing to harvest that
  you couldn't buy more cheaply as an explicit low-vol factor.
- **"Governance discount?" — MISATTRIBUTED.** What looks like a jet-governance premium is
  **betting-against-beta**: the frugal basket is low-beta staples (β 0.87), the flyer basket
  high-beta growth (β 1.31). The corporate jet is a *correlate* of the founder-growth /
  high-beta profile, not an independent, tradable red flag on this tape.
